Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/25/2026
Comments: On 8/25/2026, the Department conducted a surface inspection of the Gergely 1 well in Munster Township, Cambria County. This inspection was conducted in response to a Notice of Intent (NOI) to plug the well received on 8/18/2026.This inspection is not evaluating compliance with Order 450586, as it is being overseen by the OG SubSurface team.At the time of inspection, the following was observed:- A rig is staged on site for plugging operations. A dark, oily fluid was observed at one of the plugging rig controls. The Department recommends that the Operator monitor this portion of the plugging rig and take necessary measures to prevent a fluid release to the ground.- The access road and well site are heavily rutted, which appears to be caused by vehicles and machinery that were tracked-in for well plugging operations. No site stabilization measures, such as gravel, have been implemented anywhere on site.- It appears that no perimeter Erosion and Sedimentation (E and S) controls were installed on site prior to starting earth disturbances related to well plugging operations. No E and S/Restoration plan was observed on site during this inspection.- No evidence of a fluid leak, such as staining, was observed on the ground around the gas well. The API number was not observed on site.- The Operator's information required by OGA 3211(G) was not observed on site. The Department recommends that the Operator post their information on site in accordance with OGA 3211(G), until plugging operations are complete and the Certificate of Well Plugging (COWP) is approved by DEP Oil and Gas Inspector (OGI).Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued against the heavy tire rutting and for failure to have the E and S/Restoration plan available on site.While on site, the Department spoke via phone with Operator representative Chris Caskey and informed them of the Department's observations and forthcoming violations in this inspection report. The outstanding violations issued for failure to post the API number and operator's information on site are being overseen by the OG SubSurface team.

Inspection Date: 9/13/2022
Comments: Arrived onsite in response to a reported release of about 122 barrels of produced water.Chesapeake suspects the produced water tank onsite was struck by lightning. The produced water leaked from the bottom of the tank and was contained on the pad. The impacted area is in the southeast corner of the pad between the GPUs and containment berm. There were 2 areas of concentrated excavation but the total impacted area is expected to be less than approximately 30'x70' and about 1' deep.Conductivity measurements were performed to determine the perimeter of the impacted area and guide further excavation. At the time of inspection the area was continuing to be excavated and about 5 tri-axle loads of soil had already been removed and placed on secondary containment. The damaged tank has already been removed.Creston Environmental will collect confirmation samples to verify that the impacted area has been fully remediated. A temporary storage tank will be brought to the site to replace the damaged tank. It will be placed in front of the GPUs to keep access to the impacted area open.Violations have been cited for a release of produced water to the pad surface and Chesapeake will pursue remediation under Act 2 requirements.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 11/03/2025 to PENNHILLS RESOURCES LLC in Kingsley Township, Forest county. 102.22(b)1 - SITE STABILIZATION – TEMPORARY STABILIZATION – Permitee failed to temporarily stabilize the site to protect it from accelerated erosion and sedimentation where cessation of earth disturbance activities exceeded 4 days.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: PENNHILLS RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 11/03/2025
Violation Code: 102.22(b)1 - SITE STABILIZATION – TEMPORARY STABILIZATION – Permitee failed to temporarily stabilize the site to protect it from accelerated erosion and sedimentation where cessation of earth disturbance activities exceeded 4 days.
Violation ID: 8254678
Permit API: 053-31182
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Kingsley Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 11/03/2025
Comments: This conventional well was actively being fractured at the time of this inspection. The drilling permit and E and S Plan were posted at the entrance of the location. The access road and well site location are stoned, but due to the recent heavy traffic the road surface and site are losing their shape and stability. The road and site should be reshaped and additional clean stone considered to provide a durable road surface for continued well development on the Clinger lease. Gathering lines have been installed and backfilled within the road ditch up to this well site. Rather than grading and shaping the road ditch after the pipeline install, the backfilled material is mounded and un-stabilized. This loose fill material is at high risk for accelerated erosion and sedimentation during a rain event and is acting as a barrier for stormwater conveyance in the road ditch. The fill material within the ditch should be compacted or removed and the ditch is expected to be properly defined and temporarily stabilized in order for the ditch to function properly. The road banks and the disturbed areas around the perimeter of the well location have not been properly graded or temporarily stabilized. The road banks greatly exceed a 3:1 slope in several areas and are therefore sloughing significantly. These areas will need to be re-graded and temporarily stabilized to meet the requirements of the Chapter 102 regulations. The culvert northeast of the well location has still not been installed. Several of the culverts installed on the nearby access roads have also not been installed in accordance with the E and S Plan. The inlets of several of the culverts are plugged with fill material due to the sloughing, un-stabilized banks. The sediment plugging the culverts will need to be removed in order for them to function properly. According to the E and S Plan, stone rip-rap is expected to be placed at and below the outlet of the culvert pipes to dissipate the outfall. Infiltration berms should be installed beyond the outlet of the culverts. Several of the culvert outlets that were installed on the lease are directing stormwater towards un-stabilized fill material from the construction of the road. None of the outlets have stone rip-rap or an infiltration berm to dissipate the outfall of stormwater. These concerns will need to be addressed as outlined in the E and S Plan to meet the requirements of the Chapter 102 regulations.A follow up inspection will be conducted to ensure the above concerns have been addressed properly and in a timely manner. Due to the risk of pollution via accelerated erosion and sedimentation it is highly recommended to address these concerns prior to the next rain event.

Comments: On 6/7/22 at 1305 hrs., I conducted a follow up inspection of Stonehaven Energy Mgt. Co., LLC's Lott 2 well (API 065-26057) in Henderson Twp., Jefferson Co. A Notice of Violation was issued after an inspection conducted by WQSS Shank on 5/19/22 in which a production fluid release was documented (inspection ID 3365343, enforcement 403932). Inspection Date: 2/28/2024
Comments: This follow up inspection was conducted to evaluate the open violations at this site which were issued on November 21, 2023. The access road and site location have not been stoned. The culverts, ditches, and sumps at this location have been installed. The areas of earth disturbance along the banks of the site and access road have been mulched, however, several areas are not sufficient due to washing away over time. These areas will require added temporary stabilization. Upon arriving at the site at approximately 13:15, there was no precipitation occurring. At approximately 13:30, it began to lightly rain. It was noted that the access roads leading to the proposed wells upslope of the Hastings SDT 47 proposed well site showed evidence of accelerated erosion (see Photos 1 and 2). Due to the up slope road surface not having stone, that the up slope ditches, culverts, and sumps became overwhelmed with sediment laden water (see Photo 3). Violation ID: 999780

Unconventional: Yes

Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection of Seneca's Covington Pad R well site in Covington Township, Tioga County on 06/26/2023 at 0950. The weather was 75 degrees with overcast skies. Hydraulic stimulation activities were taking place onsite at the time of inspection. Seneca safety personnel Tighe Truman was onsite at the time of inspection.On 6/25/2023 at 0100 hours Tighe Truman of Seneca Resources notified the DEP that "Beimel Trucking was off-loading to tanks when pop-off relief valve failed spilling approximately 10 gallons of produced water to gravel. Vac truck used to recover liquid; impacted gravel scraped up and placed in bucket." The resulting spray of production fluid in front of the sites temporary storage tank offload area was estimated to be 10 gallons and encompassed roughly a 15 ft span in front of the offload area (picture 4). Steps were then taken to immediately clean the spill involving vacuuming the fluid on the pad surface and than removing impacted and stained materials from this area and storing them within the secondary containment of the temporary storage tanks until proper disposal (picture 5). The six wells onsite were undergoing hydraulic fracturing activities. Lined timber mats remain in place for the hydraulic fracturing operations. Temporary storage tanks were labeled and placed within secondary containment onsite. An Act 9 sign remains at the entrance to the site. Straw, Erosion Control Blanket (ECB), and silt sock remain in place around the pad site. Areas surrounding the pad remain stabilized as they establish vegetation. Post- Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls remain in place. No evidence of accelerated erosion or sedimentation leaving the site was observed at the time of inspection. Based on the findings of this inspection and Seneca's timely remediation of this release, violations of CSL 402(b), SWMA 301, and 25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a) are cited as immediately corrected against API # 117-22164. The DEP departed the site at 1150.

Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection conducted a Follow-up inspection of the Seneca Resources - DCNR 007 Pad K located in Delmar Twp, Tioga Co. on 7/16/2019 @1300 hours. The NOV response received on 7/15/19 from Seneca failed to provide this information. Therefore, the violations cited will remain outstanding. Seneca should reference 78a66(c) to determine the actions necessary to achieve compliance at this location. I departed the site @1400 hours.

Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 2020-05-19
Comments: Due to COVID-19 restrictions, an admin inspection is being conducted. This inspection is being conducted in response to a report submitted by the operator on May 16, 2020 at approximately 9:55 PM via the DEP hotline that a spill of approximately 10 gallons of Production Fluid occurred on the Prentice Well Pad located in Forward Township, Allegheny County. The Department contacted the operator via telephone at approximately 8:45 AM on May 18, 2020 to follow up. Based on this conversation, the operator stated that they believed a water truck was responsible for the leak, which went from the Production Tanks, across the pad, down the access road, and onto a public roadway. The operator stated that no WOTC were impacted or potentially impacted by this spill. The operator stated they had dispatched SPSI for remediation immediately, and that visibly impacted material was removed using a skid loader, the public road was cleaned up using gator-sorb. The Operator stated that remediation was completed by Sunday afternoon (May 17, 2020). The Operator mentioned that recorded video of the event from security cameras had probably caught the incident occurring. The Department is requesting any and all evidence that may have documented this incident. The Department is requesting additional information on the water truck including but not limited to, records of production fluid on the truck prior to accessing the site, how much was removed from the Production Tanks at Prentice, and the total that was off loaded after leaving the Prentice site to be submitted to the Department by 5/29/2020. The Department is also requesting how the operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted as soon as possible. Photos attached to this inspection were provided by the operator. Based on this inspection, violations are being noted as immediately corrected. Pending the operator's response, and further investigation, more violations may be issued.

Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 7/25/2022
Violation Code: 78a91(a) - PLUGGING - GENERAL PROVISIONS - Upon abandoning a well, the owner or operator failed to plug the well to stop the vertical flow of fluids or gas within the well bore under § 3221 of the 2012 Oil & Gas Act, 25 Pa. Code §§ 78a.92—78a.98 or an approved alternate method.
Violation ID: 963758
Permit API: 131-20181
Unconventional: Yes
County: Wyoming
Municipality: Lemon Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/03/2022
Comments: On site today for FUI (Follow Up Inspection) of the Karp WYO 2H. The well has been plugged by Operator. Plugging Ops. were completed on 6/20/22. When OGI Joe Gaboff performed a post plugging inspection, bubbling was heard and gas was detected at ground level from the pea gravel in cellar (See insp. ID# 3397055). - Met with Co. men (Rust Smith and Jake Peiffley) and Creston Consultants (Jason Rejan and Aden Steffe) to screen cellar and casings for gas. The cellar has been emptied of gravel and water in order to perform screenings. The conductor (20") casing is ~ 1" above the cellar floor and the surface (13 3/8") casing is ~ 6" above the conductor casing w/ a cap welded inside the top and dated. (Pic #2). - Pic #3 shows shroud sitting on the 13 3/8" surface casing and partially covering the (20x13) annulus. Meter reading (Bascom Turner Gas Explorer EGA-411) was 18% gas (peak). Creston took samples to send to lab for analysis (samples were 8% gas). Operator will share results w/ the Dept. - Later that afternoon a water truck arrived at site and filled the cellar w/ water to cover casings. Bubbling was noted from the side of the13 3/8" surface casing where an apparent slot exits vertically in the casing and extends below the welded cap. Gas screening w/ ALTAIR 5X gas meter showed bubbling contained 100% LEL and 6% CH4. - Operator will develop a corrective action plan and keep the Dept. informed of up coming activities on the Karp pad.
